m.chalisa.cau1: First I bow my head at Sāī's feet. I tell the whole story of how Sāī of Śirḍī came.
m.chalisa.cau2: Who his mother and father are, no one has ever known. Where Sāī took birth has remained a question like a riddle.
m.chalisa.cau3: Some say he is Lord Rāmacandra of Ayodhyā; some say Sāī Bābā is Hanumān, son of the Wind.
m.chalisa.cau4: Some say Sāī is Śrī Gajānana, the embodiment of blessing; some say Sāī is Devakī's son, the enchanter of Gokula.
m.chalisa.cau5: Many devotees take him for Śiva and keep worshipping Bābā; some call him an incarnation of Datta and worship Sāī.
m.chalisa.cau6: Think of him as you will, but Sāī is the true God. Most merciful, the friend of the humble, he has given the gift of life to so many.
m.chalisa.cau7: I will tell you of an event many years ago. A fortunate man's wedding party had come to Śirḍī.
m.chalisa.cau8: With it had come a very beautiful boy. Having come, he settled there and made the town of Śirḍī holy.
m.chalisa.cau9: For many days he wandered about and begged for alms from door to door; and he showed such wonders as have become immortal in the world.
m.chalisa.cau10: As his age grew, so his renown grew. In every house of the town the praises of Sāī Bābā began to be sung.
m.chalisa.cau11: Then Sāī's name began to resound in every direction, to the ends of the horizon. To protect the humble and the afflicted remained Bābā's work.
m.chalisa.cau12: Whoever went to Bābā's feet and said: I am poor, on him his mercy fell, and the bonds of his sorrow were loosed.
m.chalisa.cau13: At times someone begged: Bābā, give me a child. Then Sāī would say: So be it, and grant him the boon.
m.chalisa.cau14: Seeing the plight of the humble and afflicted, Bābā himself would grieve. Śrī Sāī's heart was as vast as the ocean.
m.chalisa.cau15: A devotee came from Madras, a man of very great wealth. His goods and treasure were beyond measure; only he had no child.
m.chalisa.cau16: He began to entreat Sāīnātha: Bābā, have mercy on me. My boat is tossed by the storm: you alone, take it across.
m.chalisa.cau17: Without a lamp of the family, darkness has fallen on my house; so I have come, Bābā, to take refuge with you.
m.chalisa.cau18: Without a lamp of the family, the show of wealth is in vain. Today, Bābā, I have come to your refuge as a beggar.
m.chalisa.cau19: Grant me the gift of a son, and I will be in your debt all my life. I hope in no one else; my trust is in you alone.
m.chalisa.cau20: He entreated and pleaded much, laying his head at his feet. Then Bābā was pleased and gave the devotee this blessing:
m.chalisa.cau21: Allāh will do you good; may a son be born in your house. His grace will remain on you and on that child of yours.
m.chalisa.cau22: To this day no one has found the limit of Sāī's grace. Giving the man from Madras a jewel of a son, he blessed his world.
m.chalisa.cau23: Whoever worships with body and mind is saved in this world. Truth has nothing to fear from the flame; falsehood is always defeated.
m.chalisa.cau24: I am always in his keeping, and I will always be his servant. I have found a Lord such as Sāī: is that by itself a small hope?
m.chalisa.cau25: I too had such a day, when I could not get bread. Clothes on my body were far away; only a tiny loincloth was left.
m.chalisa.cau26: Even with a river before me, I remained as thirsty as ever. My evil days rained a forest fire down on me.
m.chalisa.cau27: Apart from the earth, I had no support in the world. Become a beggar in the world, I was knocked about from door to door.
m.chalisa.cau28: At such a time I met a friend who was a great devotee of Sāī. He was free of entanglements, but in the world he too was like me.
m.chalisa.cau29: For the sight of Bābā the two of us took counsel together, and we made ready for the darśana of Sāī, the embodiment of compassion.
m.chalisa.cau30: In the holy town of Śirḍī we saw that enrapturing form. Our birth was blessed when we saw the form of Sāī.
m.chalisa.cau31: Since we had his darśana, all our sorrow vanished like camphor. All our troubles were wiped away, and our misfortunes came to an end.
m.chalisa.cau32: Honour and respect, all of it, we received from Bābā as alms. By Sāī's command we came to shine in the world.
m.chalisa.cau33: Bābā has given me respect, has given me honour in this life. With this as my support I will go laughing through life.
m.chalisa.cau34: Sāī's wonders had such an effect on my mind that it seems as if he fills every particle of the world.
m.chalisa.cau35: Kāśīrāma, a devotee of Bābā, lived in this Śirḍī. He would tell the world: I am Sāī's, and Sāī is mine.
m.chalisa.cau36: He sewed clothes himself and sold them in the markets of villages and towns. The strings of his heart rang with Sāī's music.
m.chalisa.cau37: The night was still; the moon and stars slept in the lap of night. Because of the darkness, one could not see one's own hand.
m.chalisa.cau38: Alas, Kāśī was coming back from the market after selling his cloth. By a very strange chance, that day he was coming alone.
m.chalisa.cau39: Crooked wrongdoers surrounded him and stood in his way. The only cry to be heard was: Beat him, cut him down, rob him.
m.chalisa.cau40: Having robbed and beaten him, the crooks made off from there. Wounded to the core by the blows, he lost consciousness.
m.chalisa.cau41: For a long time he lay there in that state. Who knows when, in some moment, a little awareness came back to him.
m.chalisa.cau42: Unknowingly the name Sāī broke from his lips, and its echo reached Bābā's ears in Śirḍī.
m.chalisa.cau43: His mind was stirred, and Bābā was in anguish. It seemed as if the whole event had taken place before his eyes.
m.chalisa.cau44: Then Bābā began to wander here and there like one frenzied. Whatever things came before him, he began to fling down.
m.chalisa.cau45: And Bābā thrust his hand into the blazing coals. All who were there grew fearful, seeing this strange tāṇḍava dance.
m.chalisa.cau46: Everyone understood that some devotee had fallen into danger. All stood there troubled, lost in wonder.
m.chalisa.cau47: It is to save him that Bābā is in anguish today; his innermost heart suffers with that man's pain.
m.chalisa.cau48: Just then fate showed its strange ways, and seeing it, the people's river of faith surged.
m.chalisa.cau49: A cart arrived there carrying the unconscious devotee. Seeing the devotee before him, Sāī's eyes filled with tears.
m.chalisa.cau50: Bābā's innermost heart was calm, steady and deep like the ocean; yet today, who knows why, again and again it was stirred.
m.chalisa.cau51: Today the very embodiment of compassion had himself become the healer, and for the devotee's sake the god had become a doorkeeper.
m.chalisa.cau52: Today Kāśī had passed the hard test of devotion. Just to see him, the townspeople came thronging.
m.chalisa.cau53: Whenever and wherever a devotee falls into danger, Bābā goes in an instant to protect him.
m.chalisa.cau54: This is the truth of every age, no new story: when a devotee is in distress, the Indweller of all hearts goes himself.
m.chalisa.cau55: Beyond all distinctions, Sāī was a worshipper of humanity. Hindus and Muslims were as dear to him as Sikhs and Christians.
m.chalisa.cau56: Bābā broke down the division between temple and mosque. Rāma and Rahīm were all his, Kṛṣṇa, Karīm and Allāh Taʿālā.
m.chalisa.cau57: Every corner of the mosque rang with the echo of the bell. Hindus and Muslims met one another, and their love grew twofold day by day.
m.chalisa.cau58: What a beautiful miracle it was, such proof this body gave of itself; and Bābā filled even the bitterness of the neem with sweetness.
m.chalisa.cau59: Sāī gave affection to all and loved all with a love beyond compare. Whatever anyone wanted, Bābā gave him that.
m.chalisa.cau60: Whoever ever repeats the name of such a vessel of affection and goodness, even if his sorrow be like a mountain, it is removed in a moment.
m.chalisa.cau61: Ah, never has anyone seen a giver like Sāī, at the mere sight of whom all misfortune went away.
m.chalisa.cau62: Sāī in the body, Sāī in the mind: worship him, repeating Sāī, Sāī. Forgetting all awareness of your own body, keep him in your thoughts.
m.chalisa.cau63: When you let go of thoughts of yourself and keep Bābā in your thoughts, and night and day repeat Bābā, Bābā, Bābā alone,
m.chalisa.cau64: then, oh, Bābā will be bound to take care of you; Bābā will have to fulfil your every wish.
m.chalisa.cau65: Do not wander from forest to forest, foolish one, searching any further for Bābā. In one place only, in Śirḍī, will you find Bābā.
m.chalisa.cau66: Blessed in the world is the soul who has found Bābā, and in sorrow or in joy, through all the eight watches, has sung Sāī's praises alone.
m.chalisa.cau67: Let mountains of troubles fall, or lightning itself strike, always take Sāī's name and stand firm before all.
m.chalisa.cau68: Hear the wonder of this old man and you will be amazed; hearing it, who knows how many clever and wise were left astonished.
m.chalisa.cau69: Once a false sādhu came to Śirḍī. He had beguiled the simple people of the town.
m.chalisa.cau70: Showing them herbs, he began to make a speech there. He began to say: Listen, my audience: my home is Vṛndāvana.
m.chalisa.cau71: I have a medicine, and there is a wondrous power in it. Simply by taking it one is freed from sorrow.
m.chalisa.cau72: If you wish to be free of trouble and disease, then my humble request to every man and every woman is this:
m.chalisa.cau73: buy it; the ways of taking it are unique. Though it is a small thing, its virtues are very great.
m.chalisa.cau74: Whoever here is childless, if he takes my medicine, oh, he will have a jewel of a son and gain the fruit he asks for.
m.chalisa.cau75: Whoever does not buy my medicine will regret it all his life. Oh, someone like me will hardly ever come here again.
m.chalisa.cau76: The world is a fair of two days; you too, enjoy yourselves. If everything is gained from this, you too, take it.
m.chalisa.cau77: The people's wonder grew as they watched his tricks; and he too was delighted within, seeing the people's simplicity.
m.chalisa.cau78: A servant ran to give Bābā this news. Hearing it, his brows knitted, and all composure left him.
m.chalisa.cau79: He commanded the servant: Seize the scoundrel at once and bring him here, or drive the cheat away beyond the bounds of Śirḍī.
m.chalisa.cau80: While I am here, who is so base as to dare to deceive the simple people of Śirḍī?
m.chalisa.cau81: In a moment I will cast such a false, deceitful, base robber into the great pit of destruction for the rest of his life.
m.chalisa.cau82: The cruel, crooked, wicked juggler got a hint that death now danced over his head, that Sāī was angry.
m.chalisa.cau83: In a moment he shut down his whole show and ran for his life. He was thinking within: O God, is there no escape now?
m.chalisa.cau84: It is true: a giver like Sāī will not be found in the world. Sāī Bābā is a part of God; nothing in the world is hard for him.
m.chalisa.cau85: Whoever, wearing the ornaments of affection, good conduct, courtesy and the like, goes forward in this world on the path of service to humanity,
m.chalisa.cau86: he alone wins the innermost heart of every person in the world; a single sorrow of his moves the whole world.
m.chalisa.cau87: Whenever the burden of sin in the world grows heavier and heavier, he comes as an incarnation, only to remove it.
m.chalisa.cau88: Taking away all the sin and injustice of this world, he drives off the world's demon in a moment.
m.chalisa.cau89: A stream of the nectar of love begins to rain on the world, and people begin to embrace one another.
m.chalisa.cau90: Just so Sāī, an incarnation, came to the mortal world and, effacing his own self, taught everyone this lesson of equality.
m.chalisa.cau91: In Śirḍī Sāī named the mosque Dvārakā. With whatever he received, Sāī wiped away sin, suffering and anguish.
m.chalisa.cau92: Sāī would always sit absorbed in the remembrance of Rāma; through all the eight watches Sāī would repeat the name of Rāma.
m.chalisa.cau93: Dry or plain, fresh or stale, or even rich dishes: to Sāī, ever hungry for love, all were the same.
m.chalisa.cau94: Whatever people gave out of their affection and faith, Bābā would partake of that food with great relish and hallow it.
m.chalisa.cau95: Sometimes, to refresh his mind, Bābā would go into the garden, and gazing on the beauty of nature he would be glad at heart.
m.chalisa.cau96: The many-coloured flowers of the garden, gently swaying, filled even a rugged, desolate mind with the water of love.
m.chalisa.cau97: Even at such a sweet hour, people stricken by sorrow, misfortune and calamity would crowd around Bābā to tell the pain of their hearts.
m.chalisa.cau98: Hearing their sad stories, his lotus eyes would fill with tears; giving them vibhūti, he would take away every pain and fill their hearts with peace.
m.chalisa.cau99: Who knows what wondrous power was in that vibhūti: those who put it on their foreheads, it took away all their sorrow.
m.chalisa.cau100: Blessed are the people who had the sight of Bābā Sāī in person; blessed are their lotus hands, with which they touched his lotus feet.
m.chalisa.cau101: Nirbhaya, if only you too had met Sāī in person, our garden, laid waste for years, would bloom again today.
m.chalisa.cau102: Had I held the feet of Śrī Sāī, I would not have let go all my life; had Sāī been displeased with me, I would surely have won him back.
